goal: Introduce one engine-owned text command processor so Console and future systems submit commands through the same interface, then interpret and process those commands at one deterministic main-thread point each frame without implementing ad-hoc per-window command execution.

checkpoints.title: Define one engine-owned command queue and submission surface
must_be_true_after: There is exactly one engine-owned text command queue for editor/runtime command submission in the process.
Command producers do not execute command logic inline anymore; they only submit text to the engine-owned queue.
The public submission API is latest-only and small: an explicit text submission entry plus a `<<` shorthand on the same owner, not a parallel wrapper hierarchy.
Submitted text is copied into processor-owned storage at the submission boundary so no cross-module STL ownership escapes the owning module.

checkpoints.title: Separate submission from interpretation and dispatch
must_be_true_after: Raw text submission, parsing, dispatch, and execution are distinct steps owned by the engine command processor instead of being mixed into ConsoleSystem.
The processor accepts text commands only in the first version; structured command objects are not introduced yet.
A built-in dispatch table exists for engine commands so help/cvar/runtime control commands are interpreted centrally.
Unknown command reporting is centralized in the processor, not duplicated in every producer.

checkpoints.title: Move Console to the unified producer path
must_be_true_after: ConsoleSystem no longer owns primary command semantics; it becomes one producer plus one output consumer for engine command results.
Submitting a line from Console enqueues text into the engine command processor through the shared API instead of calling ExecuteCommand inline.
Future systems can submit commands through the same interface with `processor << "command text"` semantics without knowing Console internals.
Console-specific UI state such as history, autocomplete, and visibility remains local to ConsoleSystem and does not leak into the processor.

checkpoints.title: Process commands at one deterministic main-thread frame point
must_be_true_after: One explicit main-thread processing phase exists per frame for engine text commands.

The preferred placement is immediately after `hooks.on_tick_ui()` and before scene pending command submission / render-pass execution in both raster and raytracing renderer loops, so commands submitted by UI in the current frame can affect the same frame deterministically.
Command draining is FIFO for one frame and bounded by an explicit per-frame policy so one producer cannot starve the frame loop accidentally.
The processing phase is shared by both raster and raytracing paths through one common hook or one common engine-owned call site instead of duplicated business logic.

checkpoints.title: Define output, errors, and validation contract
must_be_true_after: Command execution results have one engine-facing output path so Console can display them without owning execution logic.
The first implementation reports success/error/output text through a processor-owned sink contract or buffered result channel instead of direct UI calls from runtime code.
Validation stays on existing repository scripts only: build first, then use the current editor/runtime scripts instead of inventing a new command-specific harness.
The implementation plan explicitly includes regression checks for Console submission, repeated same-frame submission ordering, and cvar mutation through the unified processor.

design_notes.preferred_processing_point: Process queued text commands once per frame on the main thread immediately after hooks.on_tick_ui() and before scene pending command submission / render passes. This gives UI producers same-frame effect without moving command semantics into window code.
design_notes.preferred_submission_api: Expose one engine-owned processor with an explicit SubmitText(std::string_view) entry and an operator<<(std::string_view) shorthand on the same type. Do not add a second wrapper-only facade.
design_notes.ownership_rule: Text crossing the module boundary must be copied into processor-owned storage immediately. Do not return or transfer STL-managed command buffers across module boundaries.
design_notes.first_version_scope: Text commands only. No structured command AST, no async worker execution, no permissions model in the first landing.
design_notes.migration_rule: Console inline ExecuteCommand logic is transitional debt and should be deleted when the processor lands instead of kept as a fallback path.

validation: Planning only in this checkpoint. No implementation is part of this file.
